newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ticks higher, Sept capped at $1,600.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ticks higher, Sept capped at $1,600.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures were modestly higher in tight, rangebound trade by Monday midsession.
Volume was a tiny 523 lots up to the midday break with activity being restricted partly by lack of fresh supply/demand features.
"It's the summer period and many people are away," said one trader. "Furthermore, there are no fresh news to move the market one way or another."
Benchmark September saw its early rise capped at $1,600 on trade selling after opening unchanged at $1,590. It then closed the morning trade at $1,590 on a volume of 351 lots after a low of $1,585.
Other traded months were also higher but off their peaks.
Traders said the market was still building a base after the recent sell-off but added that it was difficult to tell the next market direction.
Chart-wise, the September contract was likely to face a small resistance at $1,612, and then a major barrier $1,650.
But Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst, said the market was more likely to come down than to go up, with the market re-testing support at just below $1,500.
The New York market also showed no clear direction although technically, strong resistance is now established at 184.50 cents a lb basis September. Support is seen at 176-175.25.
A break of the upside could probably lift the market by some 10 cents, traders said.
July 31 is the last trading day and delivery day for spot July contract.
Total original tenders to date is 2,234 lots or 11,170 tonnes, the bulk of which stopped by two major trade houses. Re-tenders totalled 1,038 lots.
On the physical front, Indonesian coffee prices continued to stay firm on the back of tight local supply. Grade four coffee was quoted at $1,550 a tonne FOB Lampung.
